newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Pro-Iraqi protesters settle old scores in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Iraqi protesters settle old scores in Gaza.

text.p: Palestinian demonstrators in Gaza turned out on Sunday to show their support for Iraq but ended up stoning each other, witnesses said.
"We sacrifice our souls and blood for you Saddam," some 100 members of Islamic and leftist factions chanted. "No, to the barbaric American attacks against the Arab Moslem Iraqi people."
But almost immediately, members of two rival factions of the pro-Iraqi Arab Liberation Party and its splinter group the Arab Liberation Party-provisional leadership began fighting, witnesses said.
"One member from each group fired bullets in the air from their pistols," one witness said. "After that both groups started throwing stones at each other. Stones came down like rain."
A Palestinian journalist was hit in the chest and arm by rocks and several cars were damaged.
Palestinian police arrived at the scene, in front of the local headquarters of the International Committee of the Red Cross, and ended the brawling, the witness said.
Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip largely backed Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait and during the 1991 Gulf War.
The PLO remained silent after last week's U.S. missile attacks on Iraq.
